subject: Social Habits
title: Sharing and taking turns
objectives: Children will share a toy with a friend with support.
Children will take turns in a simple game.
content: Sharing toys, taking turns, and waiting for my turn.
teachingActivities: Expect toddlers to say "mine"; do not force sharing but teach turns with a timer or song; praise every turn taken; keep duplicate toys available; use "my turn, your turn" language; stay close to guide gently.
learnerActivities: Share a toy with support, take turns in a simple game and wait for a short time.
assessment: Observe whether each child shares with support and waits for a turn for a short time.
expectedOutcomes: Shares a toy with adult support.
Waits for a turn for a short time.
crossCurricular: Numeracy: one each and first, next
Literacy: my turn and your turn

lessons.title: Sharing toys
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will share a toy with a friend with adult support.
successCriteria: Hands a toy to a friend with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow simple routines and use magic words with a prompt.
lessons.starter: Show the puppet holding a toy and say "I have a toy. I can share it with a friend."
teacherActivities: Show the puppet sharing a toy with another puppet.
Give two children one toy and help them share.
Praise the sharing with a smile and thank you.
learnerActivities: Child passes the toy to a friend.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the puppet sharing a toy with another puppet. Children: Children watch and say share.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Sharing makes friends happy." Children: Children smile and repeat share.
Step 3. Teacher: Give two children one toy and help them share. Children: Child passes the toy to a friend.
Step 4. Teacher: Praise the sharing with a smile and thank you. Children: Children say thank you.

practical.title: Sharing a toy
practical.safety: Use large toys without small parts and watch closely for grabbing. Never force a child to give up a toy; use turns.

differentiation.support: Hold the toy together and hand it over together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a toy to share with a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do with a toy?

lessons.conclusion: Put the toys away and say "We shared."
lessons.homeConnection: Practise sharing a snack or a toy with a sibling or friend.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "share a toy with a friend with adult support" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Sharing is caring, caring is kind.

lessons.title: Taking turns
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will take turns in a simple game.
successCriteria: Says my turn or your turn with a prompt
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow simple routines and use magic words with a prompt.
lessons.starter: Roll a soft ball to one child and say "My turn, your turn."
teacherActivities: Show how to roll the ball and say my turn.
Roll the ball to a child and say your turn.
Move around the circle with the ball.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to roll the ball and say my turn. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Roll the ball to a child and say your turn. Children: Child rolls the ball back.
Step 3. Teacher: Move around the circle with the ball. Children: Each child takes a turn.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Everyone had a turn." Children: Children clap and cheer.

practical.title: Ball turns
steps: Roll the ball to a friend.
practical.safety: Use a very soft ball and keep the circle away from hazards. Never leave a child waiting too long.

differentiation.support: Roll the ball together with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to roll the ball to a friend by name.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Takes a turn in a ball game
Uses my turn and your turn with a prompt
lessons.homeConnection: Take turns rolling a ball or stacking blocks with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "take turns in a simple game" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Waiting for my turn
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will wait for a short time for their turn.
successCriteria: Waits while a friend has a turn
Takes a turn when it is theirs
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow simple routines and use magic words with a prompt.
resources: A sand timer or a short song
A slide or toy car track
lessons.starter: Say "We wait for our turn. While we wait, we sing." and start a short song.
teacherActivities: Show how a friend has a turn on the slide or track.
Sing a short song while waiting.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how a friend has a turn on the slide or track. Children: Children watch and wait.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing a short song while waiting. Children: Children sing and wait.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Now it is your turn." Children: Child takes a turn.
Step 4. Teacher: Praise waiting with a smile. Children: Children wave or clap.

practical.title: Waiting game
steps: Stand in a line on the mat.
practical.safety: Supervise close to the slide or track and keep the line short. Never make children wait long.

differentiation.support: Wait with the child and sing quietly together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count to three while they wait.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do while we wait?

expectedOutcomes: Takes a turn when it is theirs
lessons.homeConnection: Practise waiting for a short time at the table or in a queue.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "wait for a short time for their turn" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Sharing and turns game
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will share and take turns in a small group game.
successCriteria: Shares a toy in a group
Takes a turn with a friend
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow simple routines and use magic words with a prompt.
lessons.starter: Show a basket of blocks and say "We have blocks to share. Let us build together."
teacherActivities: Show how to pass a block to a friend.
Let children take turns adding a block to a tower.
Look at the tower and say "We did it."
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to pass a block to a friend. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children take turns adding a block to a tower. Children: Child adds a block.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "My block, your block." Children: Child passes a block.
Step 4. Teacher: Look at the tower and say "We did it." Children: Children clap and cheer.

practical.title: Tower together
practical.safety: Use large, light blocks only and keep children seated safely. Watch for falling blocks.

differentiation.support: Build beside the child and take turns together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to give a block to a friend who has none.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Shares and takes turns in a group
lessons.conclusion: Put the blocks away and say "We shared."
lessons.homeConnection: Play a building game and take turns adding blocks.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "share and take turns in a small group game" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 6 sharing check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child shares and takes turns.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow simple routines and use magic words with a prompt.
lessons.starter: Sing the sharing song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: toys, ball and blocks.
At each station watch how the child shares and waits.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: toys, ball and blocks. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child shares and waits. Children: Child plays with a friend.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Sharing stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep duplicates of favourite toys. Step in gently if a child grabs.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to teach a friend to take turns.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: shares a toy; takes turns; waits for a short time; uses my turn and your turn.

questions.question: What do we do with toys?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 6
Shares and takes turns with support
lessons.homeConnection: Keep practising sharing and turns at home.
